events.text: The harvest was thin, and the store's debt book has grown fat. Half the village owes you for salt and lamp oil, and the other half is too proud to ask. The book sits on the counter between you and the window.

choices.text: Burn the debt book in the stove

effects.log: The pages go up in a puff of soot. Nobody in the village mentions it, and the next week the miller fixes your roof for nothing.

choices.text: Collect what is owed, gently and slowly

effects.log: A copper here, a copper there. By winter the book is thinner, and a few people cross the street when they see you.

choices.text: Let them pay in work instead

effects.log: The store gets a new shelf, a swept yard and a mended cart. You get to know everyone a little better.

events.text: For a week a sack of rice has been a little lighter every morning. On the eighth night you sit in the dark and wait, and the thief who comes through the back window is a girl of nine with a cloth bag and a very brave face.

choices.text: Catch her slowly, the way a shopkeeper would

effects.log: You let her run three steps before you catch her collar. By morning she is your errand-runner, paid in rice.

choices.text: Pretend to sleep, and leave a sack by the door each night

effects.log: The sacks go, one a night, all winter. In spring a basket of wild herbs appears on the step instead.

choices.text: Take her to the village headman

effects.log: The headman scolds her parents in the square. The rice stops going, and so does the girl's smile when she passes the store.

events.text: A merchant from the county town opens a second store across the well, sells everything two coppers cheaper, and sends a pair of hired thugs to stand outside yours and look at your customers.

choices.text: Lower your prices and outlast them

effects.log: It takes a lean year. In the end the merchant's cart leaves for the county town, and the thugs go with it.

choices.text: Invite the merchant to tea and talk it through

ok.log: Two pots of tea later you have a partner, not a rival: the merchant brings goods from town and you sell them.

fail.log: The merchant drinks your tea and raises the thugs' pay. It is a long winter at the counter.

choices.text: Let one of the thugs trip over a rice sack

effects.log: He lands on his back in the street, very hard, and cannot work out how. Neither of them comes back. People do look at you a little longer.

events.text: A young swordsman with a sect badge and no money to speak of orders a sword. You could make him the best blade on this road with your eyes shut. A village smith could not.

choices.text: Make him an honest village blade

effects.log: It is plain, true and heavy. He is a little disappointed, and the sword will still be in one piece when he is old.

choices.text: Fold it a hundred times anyway

effects.log: The blade sings when he draws it. By spring three sects have sent someone to ask who the smith of this village really is.

choices.text: Tell him you only make ploughs

effects.log: He leaves for the county town. You spend the afternoon on a plough, and find there is a whole Dao in getting the angle right.

events.text: The temple's great bell has cracked in the frost. The abbot has no silver for a bell-founder, and asks, without much hope, whether a village smith might recast it.

choices.text: Recast it by hand over a month of nights

effects.log: You build the mould in the temple yard and pour it at dawn. The first stroke rolls over the valley, and the abbot weeps.

choices.text: Do it for a fair price

effects.log: The temple pays in instalments for two years. The bell sounds the same either way.

choices.text: Teach the novices to do it with you

effects.log: Twelve novices, one furnace and a great deal of shouting. The bell is a little out of tune, and they are very proud of it.

events.text: An orphan boy has been sitting outside the forge every day for a month, watching the hammer. Today he asks to be your apprentice. He has the shoulders for it, and a stubbornness that reminds you of someone.

choices.text: Take him on

effects.log: He burns himself twice in the first week and never complains. By the end of the year he can make a hinge that does not squeak.

choices.text: Teach him the hammer, and never the breath behind it

effects.log: You teach only what a smith knows. He will never know there was more, and he is happy. You think about that a long time.

choices.text: Send him to a real martial school in the county town

effects.log: You write him a letter of introduction in a mortal's clumsy hand. Years later you hear he made First-Rate.

events.text: A fever comes up the river with the spring boats. Six houses, then twenty. One needle of qi in the right place would break it in a night, and every master in the province would hear of the doctor who did it.

choices.text: Fight it the mortal way, day and night

effects.log: Willow bark, boiled water and no sleep for a month. Two old people die. Everyone else lives, and you are thin as a rake.

choices.text: Climb the mountain for stronger herbs

effects.log: Three days on the cliffs for a root most doctors only read about. The fever breaks within the week.

choices.text: Close the clinic and keep your head down

effects.log: You stay inside with the shutters closed. The fever passes on its own, and the village does not knock on your door the same way again.

events.text: Midnight, a storm, and the miller's daughter has been in labour since noon. The midwife is across the flooded river. The house is full of frightened people looking at you.

choices.text: Do it yourself, by lamplight

ok.log: At dawn a red-faced boy is yelling at the whole house. His mother names him after the doctor.

fail.log: It is a terrible night. By morning mother and child are both alive, just, and you are shaking.

choices.text: Send the strongest swimmer for the midwife

effects.log: The miller's son swims the river and comes back with the midwife on his back. You hold the lamp. It is enough.

events.text: The magistrate's son is coughing blood, and the county physicians call it consumption. It is not. It is Seven-Night Frost, a poison only a martial artist would know, which means someone in that house is one.

choices.text: Name the poison, and let them wonder how you know

effects.log: The boy lives. The magistrate looks at you for a long moment, and then decides not to ask.

choices.text: Cure it quietly and call it luck

effects.log: A bitter tea for a month. The boy recovers, and you leave a note under the poisoner's door that says only: I know.

choices.text: Treat the cough and take the fee

effects.log: The cough eases for a season. You hear in the autumn that the boy did not see the winter, and you do not sleep well for a while.

events.text: A table of travellers is telling a story about a great master of the jianghu who vanished. The master is you. According to them you ascended in a pillar of light, or were poisoned by a jealous lover, depending on who is drinking.

choices.text: Correct one small detail, and laugh

effects.log: "That one was never jealous," you say, refilling a cup. The table roars, and the story gets better every night.

choices.text: Pour another round and let them tell it

effects.log: You learn more about yourself in one evening than in a year of seclusion. Very little of it is true.

choices.text: Ask what they think became of that master

effects.log: An old carter says, "Got tired, I expect. Even masters get tired." You think about that for a week.

events.text: A First-Rate brawler from some sect drinks too much, throws a table through the wall and starts on the guests. He is nothing. And you cannot lift a finger against him without breaking the seal.

choices.text: Refuse him more wine, politely and firmly

ok.log: Something in your voice makes him put the cup down. He pays for the wall and never comes back.

fail.log: He shoves you into the bar hard enough to crack it. A mortal would have broken a rib. You pretend you have.

choices.text: Water his wine until he falls asleep

effects.log: Four jugs of mostly water later he is snoring under a table, and the guests are laughing at him instead of running.

choices.text: Let it pass, and mend the tables in the morning

effects.log: You mend the wall and three tables. It costs you a month's takings and nothing else, which is a strange feeling.

events.text: You find a young disciple of a great sect hiding in your stable in torn robes, a runaway from an arranged match and a master who would not listen. The sect's riders are two villages behind.

choices.text: Hide them in the cellar

effects.log: The riders search the inn and find wine. By the time they leave, the runaway is three valleys away with your second-best cloak.

choices.text: Send word to the sect

effects.log: The riders take the runaway home. The sect sends you a letter of thanks and a box of tea that tastes of nothing.

choices.text: Give them supper, and a talk about the road

effects.log: You tell them what the road is really like. In the morning they go home on their own feet, to argue properly.

events.text: The lantern festival, and the village elders ask you to carry the head of the paper dragon through the streets. It weighs nothing at all to you. It is supposed to weigh a great deal.

choices.text: Carry it, puffing like a mortal

effects.log: You stagger convincingly the whole length of the street. The children chase the dragon and scream with joy. It is the best night in years.

choices.text: Light the lanterns in the square instead

effects.log: Four hundred lanterns, one by one. When the last is lit you stand in the middle of them and feel very ordinary, and very glad.

choices.text: Watch from your doorway

effects.log: From the doorway you can see the whole village at once, every face lit from below. You understand something about why people build villages.

events.text: Old Granny Pak from next door is dying, and asks for you. She holds your hand and says, "You have never been only who you say you are. I do not mind. But tell me, before I go."

choices.text: Tell her the truth, quietly

effects.log: She listens to all of it and laughs, a small dry laugh. "I knew it," she says. "Nobody carries rice like that." She dies smiling.

choices.text: Tell her a kind story instead

effects.log: You tell her you were once a poor scholar who failed the examinations. She pats your hand as if she believes it.

choices.text: Hold her hand and say nothing

effects.log: You sit with her until the lamp burns down. She does not ask again. Perhaps she did not need to.

events.text: The spring flood comes over the levee at night. The whole village is out with baskets of earth, in the rain, and the river is winning.

choices.text: Work through the night like everyone else

effects.log: You carry earth until dawn at a mortal's pace, and your arms ache the way they have not ached in a century. The levee holds.

choices.text: Organise the village into lines

effects.log: Lines of passing hands, the old at the back, the young at the front. The levee holds, and the headman asks you to sit on the council.

choices.text: Save the stock in your own shop first

effects.log: Your shelves stay dry. Two houses on the river side do not, and their families notice where you were.

events.text: You have lived here long enough that the children you sold sweets to are buying sweets for their own children. Your face has not changed. The village has started to whisper.

choices.text: Dye grey into your hair

effects.log: A little ash and indigo every morning. The whispering stops. You feel a little silly, and a little safer.

choices.text: Let them whisper

effects.log: By spring there is a story that you once saved a mountain spirit, who blessed you. It is not far wrong, in its way.

choices.text: Tell them it runs in the family

effects.log: "My grandmother looked forty at ninety," you say. Everyone nods. Everyone has a grandmother like that.

events.text: {npc} ducks under your awning to get out of a summer storm, soaked to the skin, and laughs at the state of your umbrella, which has three ribs left. It is the first time in years anyone has laughed at you.

choices.text: Offer {him} tea until the rain stops

mem.note: gave me tea in the rain

effects.log: The rain lasts all afternoon. So does the conversation.

choices.text: Lend {him} the terrible umbrella

mem.note: lent me a terrible umbrella

effects.log: The umbrella comes back the next day, mended, with a sweet bun tied to the handle.

choices.text: Nod politely and close the shutters

effects.log: The storm passes. You sit in the dim shop and tell yourself it is better this way.

events.text: Market day, and {npc} haggles with you over a sack of millet as if {his} life depended on it. {He} is wrong about the price, wrong about the weather, and the most interesting person you have spoken to in a decade.

choices.text: Haggle back with real pleasure

mem.note: haggled with me for an hour

effects.log: An hour later neither of you has won, and {npc} comes back the next market day for no reason at all.

choices.text: Give {him} the price {he} asks

mem.note: let me win at the market

effects.log: {He} looks at you suspiciously, as if you had cheated somehow, and smiles despite {him}self.

choices.text: Keep it to business

effects.log: You sell the millet at a fair price. {He} does not come to your stall again.

events.text: An evening walk along the river with {npc}, which has become a habit neither of you talks about. Tonight {he} asks where you really came from, because nobody comes from nowhere.

choices.text: Tell a true thing that is not the whole truth

mem.note: told me about the mountains

effects.log: You tell {him} about the mountain where you grew up, and the old teacher, and leave out everything that would frighten {him}.

choices.text: Make up a past, a dull and safe one

mem.note: told me a story about the south

effects.log: A failed scholar from the south. {He} nods along. You suspect {he} does not believe a word.

choices.text: Step back: you will outlive {him} by a century

effects.log: You say you are tired and walk home alone. You are right, and it does not help at all.

events.text: {npc} falls ill with the winter fever. It is nothing to you, a few days of sweating for a mortal, unless it turns. You find you are counting {his} breaths.

choices.text: Sit by {him} every night until it breaks

mem.note: sat by me every night of the fever

effects.log: Seven nights. On the eighth morning {he} wakes, sees you asleep in the chair, and does not wake you.

choices.text: Pay for the best physician in the county

mem.note: sent for a physician for me

effects.log: The physician is pompous and expensive and quite good. {npc} recovers, and is embarrassed about the cost for a month.

choices.text: Send a neighbour to look in, and keep away

effects.log: The fever breaks on its own. When {npc} is well again, {he} nods to you in the street, and only nods.

events.text: Under the old elm in the square, with half the village pretending not to watch, {npc} asks you plainly whether you mean to marry {him} or not, because {he} is not getting any younger, and neither, {he} says, looking at you oddly, are you.

choices.text: Say yes

mem.note: said yes under the elm

effects.log: The half of the village that was pretending not to watch starts cheering.

choices.text: Say not yet

mem.note: said not yet under the elm

effects.log: {He} looks at you for a long time, and says {he} will ask once more, and only once.

choices.text: Say you cannot, and that you cannot say why

mem.note: would not marry me and would not say why

effects.log: {He} walks away without a word. The elm is very quiet after that.

events.text: Lantern night again, and this time you are the one who means to ask. You have faced masters who could split mountains. Your hands have never shaken like this.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to marry you

mem.note: asked me on lantern night

effects.log: {He} says yes before you have finished the question, and then makes you finish it anyway.

choices.text: Lose your nerve and talk about the weather

mem.note: talked about the weather on lantern night

effects.log: You talk about the weather for an hour. {npc} lets you, which is either kindness or cruelty.

choices.text: Decide a mortal deserves someone who will grow old beside {him}

effects.log: You let the lanterns float away unasked. It is the right thing, probably. It does not feel like anything at all.

events.text: {npc}, your own disciple, stops at your counter on the road, travel-stained and older, and does not know you. {He} is asking every village on this road about a master who vanished years ago.

choices.text: Sell {him} what {he} needs and say nothing

effects.log: {He} thanks the shopkeeper politely and walks on. You watch {him} to the bend in the road, and further.

choices.text: Correct {his} stance with a word, as an old shopkeeper might

mem.note: fixed my stance from behind a shop counter

effects.log: "Your weight is on the wrong foot," you say. {He} stares at you. Then {he} laughs, and fixes it, and goes on {his} way puzzled.

choices.text: Let {him} see you

mem.note: found my master in a village shop

effects.log: {He} drops everything {he} is carrying and kneels in the dust of the road.

events.text: {npc}, your own disciple, staggers into the village at dusk with an arrow in the shoulder and riders not far behind, and falls against your door without knowing whose it is.

choices.text: Treat {him} as a mortal would, and hide {him}

mem.note: hid me in a village

effects.log: The riders search the street and move on. {He} sleeps for two days in your back room, and leaves a coin on the pillow.

choices.text: Tell {him} where the riders will look

mem.note: told me which road to take

effects.log: You know exactly how hunters think. {He} takes the river path, and gets away, wondering how a shopkeeper knew.

choices.text: Break the seal and end the pursuit

mem.note: came back to save me

effects.log: The riders see the shopkeeper step into the road, and then they see something else, and they turn their horses around.

events.text: Three young martial artists drink at your counter and boast about the great master they are going to defeat one day and make their name on. They have the name wrong in two places, but it is yours.

choices.text: Laugh along with them

effects.log: You pour them another round on the house. "To the day you find that master," you say, and they cheer.

choices.text: Give them advice dressed as an old proverb

effects.log: "The one who wants a name loses a fight before it starts," you say. The youngest one writes it on his sleeve.

choices.text: Let one of them feel your gaze for a heartbeat

effects.log: The loudest one goes white and spills his wine. They leave early, and talk about the strange shopkeeper all the way down the road.

events.text: Disciples in the colours of a great sect come through the village hunting a demonic cultivator, kicking doors in and frightening everyone. Their quarry is hiding in the mill. You felt it arrive an hour ago.

choices.text: Point the way with a trembling hand, like a mortal

effects.log: They find the mill and the fight is short. The village sweeps up after them, as villages do.

choices.text: Gather the frightened villagers into the temple

effects.log: Nobody is hurt but the mill door. The abbot thanks you, and nobody thinks it odd that the shopkeeper was so calm.

choices.text: Break the seal and end it before anyone is hurt

effects.log: The demonic cultivator never leaves the mill. The disciples stand in the street staring at you for a long time.

events.text: Smoke on the north road at dawn: the Black Wind bandits, three hundred riders, and this village is the next on their way. The headman is ringing the bell. Nobody here has ever held a sword.

choices.text: Break the seal and stand in the gate

effects.log: You walk out to meet three hundred riders alone, and the village watches the shopkeeper they thought they knew stop being one.

choices.text: Stay hidden, and lead the villagers into the hills

ok.log: You know every goat path above the village. By morning everyone is safe in the caves, and nobody asks how you knew them all.

fail.log: The path is found. You get most of them out, and take a blow meant for a child, and the village loses its granary.

choices.text: Stay hidden behind your counter

effects.log: You bar the door and sit in the dark with the seal shut, and listen.

events.text: Two great sects at war have chosen the fields outside the village for their battle. Arrays light up the night, and stray sword-qi has already taken the roof off the miller's house.

choices.text: Break the seal and stand in the gate

effects.log: You walk out to meet two armies of martial artists alone, and the village watches the shopkeeper they thought they knew stop being one.

choices.text: Stay hidden, and lead the villagers into the hills

ok.log: You know every goat path above the village. By morning everyone is safe in the caves, and nobody asks how you knew them all.

fail.log: The path is found. You get most of them out, and take a blow meant for a child, and the village loses its granary.

choices.text: Stay hidden behind your counter

effects.log: You bar the door and sit in the dark with the seal shut, and listen.

events.text: A column of the Heavenly Demon Cult comes over the pass to take the young of the valley for their cult. The villagers are hiding their children in rice jars.

choices.text: Break the seal and stand in the gate

effects.log: You walk out to meet a column of the Demonic Cult alone, and the village watches the shopkeeper they thought they knew stop being one.

choices.text: Stay hidden, and lead the villagers into the hills

ok.log: You know every goat path above the village. By morning everyone is safe in the caves, and nobody asks how you knew them all.

fail.log: The path is found. You get most of them out, and take a blow meant for a child, and the village loses its granary.

choices.text: Stay hidden behind your counter

effects.log: You bar the door and sit in the dark with the seal shut, and listen.

events.text: An army of deserters, starving and armed, comes down the valley taking every grain store and burning what they cannot carry. The village has one winter's food and nothing else.

choices.text: Break the seal and stand in the gate

effects.log: You walk out to meet an army with nothing left to lose alone, and the village watches the shopkeeper they thought they knew stop being one.

choices.text: Stay hidden, and lead the villagers into the hills

ok.log: You know every goat path above the village. By morning everyone is safe in the caves, and nobody asks how you knew them all.

fail.log: The path is found. You get most of them out, and take a blow meant for a child, and the village loses its granary.

choices.text: Stay hidden behind your counter

effects.log: You bar the door and sit in the dark with the seal shut, and listen.

events.text: A letter finds you at last, after years on the road, addressed in an old hand to a name nobody here has ever called you. Whoever wrote it knows exactly who you were, and asks you to come back.

choices.text: Go back

effects.log: You read it three times, fold it into your sleeve, and start putting the shop in order.

choices.text: Burn it unread, and stay

effects.log: The letter curls up in the stove. Whatever it wanted, the shop is open in the morning.

choices.text: Write back that the one they want is dead

effects.log: You write it carefully, in a mortal's clumsy hand. It is almost true.

events.text: You dream of the peak where you trained, the wind on it, the stone under your knees, every form you ever learned unfolding at once. You wake with your hands in the shape of the first form, and the sealed energy stirring.

choices.text: Pack, and go back to the peak

effects.log: You are on the road before the village wakes, and you do not look back until the bend.

choices.text: Get up and open the shop as usual

effects.log: You make the tea and open the shutters. The energy settles, and so do you.

choices.text: Sit with the dream until it fades

effects.log: You sit on the step until the sun is up and the dream is only a dream again.

events.text: You close the year's accounts by lamplight and find they balance to the copper, the way they have every year for a long time now. The life here is complete. That is either a reason to stay or a reason to go.

choices.text: A reason to go

effects.log: You close the book and know, quite calmly, that it is time.

choices.text: A reason to stay

effects.log: You open next year's book and write the date at the top, very neatly.

choices.text: Leave the question for next year

effects.log: You blow out the lamp. The question will still be there. So will you.

events.text: That night {npc} sets out two cups, pours the tea, and waits, with {his} hands folded, for you to explain who {he} has been married to all these years.

choices.text: Tell {him} everything

mem.note: told me the truth at last

effects.log: It takes until dawn. At the end {he} says only, "That explains the rice sacks."

choices.text: Ask {him} to come with you into the jianghu

mem.note: asked me to come along

effects.log: {He} thinks about it for a long time. "Someone has to keep the shop," {he} says. "Come home in winter."

choices.text: Promise to come home every winter

mem.note: promised to come home every winter

effects.log: {He} nods, and pours you another cup, and holds you to it.

events.text: "I always knew," {npc} says, before you can begin. "Not what, exactly. But nobody mortal mends a roof in the rain without getting wet."

choices.text: Laugh, and tell {him} the rest

mem.note: laughed and told me the rest

effects.log: You laugh until you both cry. Then you tell {him} the rest, and {he} listens like someone hearing a very long story {he} already likes.

choices.text: Ask why {he} never said anything

mem.note: asked why I never said

effects.log: "Because you were happy," {he} says. "Why would I spoil it?"
